accepted.explanation: 지문은 윤리적 사고가 증거와 쟁점을 여러 관점에서 평가하는 과정이라고 정의하며, 정해진 윤리 규칙을 따르는 것과 구분한다. 또한 어떤 행동이 윤리적인지는 개인마다, 나아가 같은 사람에게서도 상황과 시기에 따라 달라진다고 설명한다. 따라서 학생들은 고정 규칙을 암기하기보다 다양한 관점으로 윤리 문제를 살피고, 개인 행동 규범이 맥락 의존적임을 이해해야 한다. 이에 가장 알맞은 쌍은 multiple perspectives / context-dependent이다.

accepted.explanation: 지문은 소형·저기술 제품에서는 personal flair가 필수인 반면, 대규모 프로젝트에서는 다수의 디자이너가 개념을 구현하므로 유명 ‘개성’ 디자이너도 사실상 creative manager로 기능한다고 본다. 따라서 그룹 작업에서는 management organization and processes가 designers' creativity만큼 중요하다고 결론짓는다. 이를 요약하면 소형 제품의 (A) flair와 그룹 실무의 (B) organizational processes 대조가 정답이며, 한쪽만 맞는 선지(2, 3)는 이 전역 관계를 놓친다.

wrongOptionExplanations.4: 직전 문장이 이미 '일을 할 수 없다'는 확신을 다루므로 delay는 그보다 앞 단계여야 하며, 직후 '(You are correct.)'가 delay의 결과로 읽히면 논리 순서가 거꾸로 된다.

accepted.explanation: 주어진 문장의 As a result는 위험·탐색을 회피하고 마음에 맞는 일에서 멀어지는 행동의 결과로 지연이 따른 자리를 가리킨다. 그 앞에 'away from risk and exploration, and possibly further from the work of your heart'가 있어야 결과 관계가 성립하고, 그 뒤에 'Believing that your work should be perfect, you gradually become convinced that you cannot do it'이 이어져 지연이 무능력 확신으로 심화되는 흐름이 닫힌다. 그 외 자리에서는 원인 부재, 단계 역전, 또는 이미 끊긴 응집이 발생한다.

accepted.passageWithMarkers: To require perfection is to invite paralysis. ① The pattern is predictable: as you see error in what you have done, you steer your work toward what you imagine you can do perfectly. ② You cling ever more tightly to what you already know you can do ― away from risk and exploration, and possibly further from the work of your heart. ③ Believing that your work should be perfect, you gradually become convinced that you cannot do it. (You are correct.) Sooner or later, since you cannot do what you are trying to do, you quit. ④ And in one of those little ironies of life, only the pattern itself achieves perfection ― a perfect death spiral: you misdirect your work; you stall; you quit. ⑤

accepted.direction: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
sentences: The very features that create expertise in a specialized domain lead to ignorance in many others.
In some cases lay people ― farmers, fishermen, patients, native peoples ― may have relevant experiences that scientists can learn from.
Indeed, such experiences among lay people show that everyday observation is often more reliable than the specialized domain of experts.
Indeed, in recent years, scientists have begun to recognize this: the Arctic Climate Impact Assessment includes observations gathered from local native groups.

But without some degree of trust in our designated experts ― the men and women who have devoted their lives to sorting out tough questions about the natural world we live in ― we are paralyzed, in effect not knowing whether to make ready for the morning commute or not.

wrongOptionExplanations.①: 전문 영역의 전문성이 다른 영역 무지로 이어진다는 핵심 근거를 제시해 도입 논지를 뒷받침하므로 흐름에 맞다.
wrongOptionExplanations.②: 일부 경우 비전문가 경험이 과학자에게 배움이 될 수 있다는 보완 사례로, 한정된 신뢰 논의로 이어진다.
wrongOptionExplanations.④: 바로 앞 주장을 구체 사례(북극평가의 원주민 관찰 반영)로 확인하는 문장이라 연결이 자연스럽다.
wrongOptionExplanations.⑤: 전문가를 전혀 믿지 않으면 일상 판단마저 마비된다는 결론으로, 제한적이되 필요한 신뢰라는 주제를 마무리한다.

accepted.explanation: 글의 흐름은 전문 영역이 다른 영역의 무지를 낳을 수 있지만, 비전문가 경험을 제한적으로 참고하면서도 지정 전문가에 대한 필요한 신뢰를 유지해야 한다는 쪽으로 전개된다. 'Indeed, such experiences among lay people...'로 시작하는 문장은 lay people, experiences, specialized domain 등 주변 어휘를 이어받아 연결된 듯 보이지만, 일상 관찰이 전문 영역보다 더 신뢰할 만하다고 평가를 뒤집어 전문가 신뢰의 필요성이라는 중심 논리를 흔든다. 이 문장만 빼면 비전문가 경험 인식 사례로 바로 이어져 문단이 매끄럽다.
keyPoints: 무관 문장은 주제어를 공유하되 담화 기능(평가)만 어긋나는 함정으로 만든다.
전문가 한계 인정과 비전문가 참고 가능성을 말한 뒤, 필요한 신뢰로 귀결되는 글의 구조를 파악한다.
제거 후 앞뒤가 자연히 이어지는 remove-and-reconnect 시험을 적용해 정답을 확인한다.
accepted.passageWithNumbers: Scientists have no special purchase on moral or ethical decisions; a climate scientist is no more qualified to comment on health care reform than a physicist is to judge the causes of bee colony collapse. ① __The very features that create expertise in a specialized domain lead to ignorance in many others.__ ② __In some cases lay people ― farmers, fishermen, patients, native peoples ― may have relevant experiences that scientists can learn from.__ ③ __Indeed, such experiences among lay people show that everyday observation is often more reliable than the specialized domain of experts.__ ④ __Indeed, in recent years, scientists have begun to recognize this: the Arctic Climate Impact Assessment includes observations gathered from local native groups.__ So our trust needs to be limited, and focused. It needs to be very particular. Blind trust will get us into at least as much trouble as no trust at all. ⑤ __But without some degree of trust in our designated experts ― the men and women who have devoted their lives to sorting out tough questions about the natural world we live in ― we are paralyzed, in effect not knowing whether to make ready for the morning commute or not.__

accepted.direction: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
sentences: In highly representational paintings, plays, or stories, the focus is on subject matter that resembles everyday life and the role of background style is to facilitate the construction of mental models.
Indeed, the background style that facilitates the construction of mental models can become the very focus that makes such works more closely resemble everyday life for the viewer.
Feelings of pleasure and uncertainty carry the viewer along to the conclusion of the piece.

Thus, when the work is less "readable" (or easily interpreted), its departure from conventional forms reminds the viewer or reader that an "aesthetic attitude" is needed to appreciate the whole episode.
An ability to switch between the "pragmatic attitude" of everyday life and an "aesthetic attitude" is fundamental to a balanced life.

wrongOptionExplanations.①: 재현적 작품에서 소재와 배경 양식의 역할을 구분·정의하며, 글의 첫 대조축을 세우는 문장이므로 흐름상 필수이다.
wrongOptionExplanations.③: 재현적 작품이 보는 이를 쾌락과 불확실성으로 결말까지 이끈다는 후속 설명으로, 앞 정의 문장과 자연스럽게 이어진다.
wrongOptionExplanations.④: 표현주의 작품이 관습적 형식에서 벗어나 미적 태도를 요구한다는 요지를 잇는 핵심 연결 문장이다.
wrongOptionExplanations.⑤: 실용적 태도와 미적 태도를 전환하는 능력이 균형 잡힌 삶에 근본적이라는 글의 결론을 담아 필수이다.

accepted.explanation: 지문은 재현적 작품에서 배경 양식(style)이 정신 모형 구축을 '보조'하고 소재(subject matter)가 초점이라는 역할 분리를 전제한 뒤, 표현주의 작품의 조화롭지 않은 양식·미적 태도 요구·태도 전환의 중요성으로 나아간다. 'Indeed, the background style that facilitates...'로 시작하는 문장은 background style, facilitate the construction of mental models, resemble everyday life 등 앞 문장의 핵심 어휘를 이어받아 표면상 연결되지만, 보조 수단이어야 할 배경 양식을 초점이 되어 일상과 더 닮게 만든다고 역할을 뒤집어 평가를 역전시킨다. 이 문장만 빼면 앞의 역할 정의가 바로 쾌락·불확실성 문장으로 매끄럽게 이어진다.
keyPoints: 무관문은 중심 소재어를 공유해도 문단의 논리 기능(역할 분배)이 어긋나면 탈락한다.
바로 앞 문장의 어휘·지시 연결로 '이어진 척' 하지만 배경 양식의 조연 역할을 주연으로 뒤집은 평가 역전을 찾는다.
무관문 제거 시 앞뒤 원문이 빈틈없이 이어지는 remove-and-reconnect 검사를 한다.

accepted.direction: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
accepted.givenSentence: Garcia stood outside Frontcountry Mall, waiting for his brother, Jeff. Garcia's band had been chosen to perform at the welcoming ceremony for a large group of students from their sister university in Singapore.

paragraphs.label: (A)
paragraphs.text: Garcia felt good as he arrived at the concert hall for the rehearsal wearing his new clothes. His confidence was, however, quickly changed to nervousness when he thought of how many people would be there. As the rehearsal began, he struggled with the rhythm, making several mistakes. Tom, Garcia's band mate, came over and put a hand on Garcia's back, saying, "Don't worry, I'll be right behind you." He looked at his friend, took a deep breath and started to feel much better.

paragraphs.label: (B)
paragraphs.text: "Aren't these cool?" Garcia asked, pointing at a patterned red shirt and yellow pants he had found in the store. "Um, I think they're a bit too colorful," Jeff objected. Instead, Jeff picked out a white shirt and black jeans. He asked the store clerk, "Don't you think these would look great on my brother?" The clerk stopped her work and looked at the clothes, quickly agreeing with Jeff's choice. Garcia bought the recommended clothes, saying, "Maybe I'll wear these for tonight's rehearsal, too."

paragraphs.label: (C)
paragraphs.text: Garcia was hoping to find the perfect clothing for the performance. That was why he had asked Jeff to help him pick out new clothes. "I'm sorry. I'm late because traffic was terrible," Jeff apologized as he arrived. "Don't worry. I haven't waited long," Garcia replied as they entered the lively shopping center.

accepted.passageWithBlank: Carol was new to the United States. One of her friends called to invite her to lunch. She offered to pick her up on the corner of 34th Street and Fifth Avenue at 11:30 a.m. Carol arrived a little early and was standing on the corner waiting for her friend when she noticed a sign above her head. It said, "No Standing." Carol didn't know what to do. She moved away from the sign and started walking back and forth on the street. She was happy to see her friend arrive and couldn't wait to get into her car. She excitedly explained that it was a bad idea to meet at that corner because people aren't allowed to stand there. Her friend said, "What are you talking about? Of course you can stand there." "No," she said, "the sign says 'No Standing'." Her friend burst into laughter. "That means _____."

accepted.passageWithMarkers: Environmental taxes based directly on measured emissions can, in principle, be very precisely targeted to the policy's environmental objectives. ① If a firm pollutes more, it pays additional tax directly in proportion to the rise in emissions. ② The polluter thus has an incentive to reduce emissions in any manner that is less costly per unit of abatement than the tax on each unit of residual emissions. ③ The great attraction of basing the tax directly on measured emissions is that the actions the polluter can take to reduce tax liability are actions that also reduce emissions. ④ Nevertheless, the technologies available for monitoring the concentrations and flows of particular substances in waste discharges have been developing rapidly. In the future, it may be possible to think of taxing measured emissions in a wider range of applications. ⑤

accepted.passageWithBlank: I can report a number of occasions when my own dogs reacted in a marked, I would say enthusiastic, manner when I wore jingling jewelry that produced a regular rhythm as I walked, though admittedly they did not tap their feet. Although this is a mere anecdote, it suggests that it is wrong to claim that animals are incapable of responding to pronounced rhythms. The specific response of tapping one's foot or deliberately marking any external rhythm does seem to be a particularly human skill, but this need not be interpreted as _____. My dogs in fact responded to other musical features beside the regular jingling of my jewelry. The sound of a siren would set them to howling, as would the sound of my husband's saxophone. Perhaps Aristotle observed similar reactions of dogs to musical instruments and rhythms. Apparently Darwin did. He reports observing a dog that was "always whining, when one note on a concertina, which was out of tune, was played."
